requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).
verdict_reason: 1 test(s) fail on head (passing on base, or added by the change): GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 169/170 passed, 1 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The new README section and MsgPack004 doc state that diagnostics for metadata-only types are reported by the defining assembly and that the consumer does not analyse them. This is deliberate per the ledger, not a defect. The dropped diagnostics and the lack of a consumer-side formatter for such types match the recorded behaviour.
Receipts/Req2283ReferencedGenericStructTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-2
Receipts/MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticsTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed
Mutation not meaningful: the selected tests already fail on head

findings.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` claims to drop diagnostics about metadata members, but it only drops diagnostics that have a source location in another compilation. For a member of a PE-referenced type, the new `FirstOrDefault()` / `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` calls return null, so `Diagnostic.Create` gets `Location.None`. `Location.None.IsInSource` is false, so the guard `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || ...` passes and the diagnostic is reported. Concrete input: `lib` (built without the MessagePack analyzer, e.g. analyzer assets excluded, F#, or an older package) declares `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> { [Key(0)] public string Key {get;set;} public int Unkeyed {get;set;} }`; `app` uses `Item<int>` as a keyed member. On base this crashed. On head the consuming assembly gets a location-less MsgPack004 (an Error, L2) about a type it does not own. The same applies to MsgPack003/BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and other Location.None reports. This contradicts L8 (the defining assembly owns validating its own types) and breaks the app build instead of producing a clean one.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticsTests.MetadataGenericStruct_UnkeyedMember_NotReportedInConsumer. It emits Lib to a PE image, references it from App, and runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer. It asserts no MsgPack004 is reported. Expected to fail on head with a MsgPack004 at Location.None.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only drops diagnostics whose Location is in source but belongs to another compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None (metadata/null location, e.g. from FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() returning null) have IsInSource false and are still reported. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 (an Error per L2) for a member lacking [Key] is now emitted with no location in the user's build. Previously the type would crash; now a metadata type that lacks keys could fail the user's build with a location-less error, contradicting L8 (referenced types are deliberately not analysed).

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer/generator test: lib defines generic struct Item<T> with a public member lacking [Key]/[IgnoreMember] inside [MessagePackObject], compiled to a metadata reference; app has Cmd with Item<int> member. Assert no MsgPack004 diagnostic (or any Location.None diagnostic) is reported in app. Expect failure with the current filter since !IsInSource is true.

hunches.claim: The new filter is applied to all reportDiagnostic calls in TypeCollector, not just the crashing paths. Any diagnostic previously reported with a location in a different syntax tree/compilation is now silently dropped. Existing users could lose diagnostics they used to see, such as source-declared types in another compilation or linked/multi-project cases. This is a behavior change for analyzer output without opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003/004/005/etc. tests) at head and compare against base; add a case where the diagnostic location is in a tree not in compilation.SyntaxTrees and verify whether the diagnostic was previously reported.

hunches.claim: The wrapper that drops diagnostics whose location is outside the compilation is installed for every analyzer diagnostic, not just the metadata-symbol paths. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None), where IsInSource is false, still pass through. Diagnostics anchored in another syntax tree are silently suppressed. This broad filter could hide wrong or valid reports, and L10 notes the analyzer has been sensitive to false positives. The tests only cover the unkeyed-member case, not other diagnostics (MsgPack003/005) against the filter.

receipt_plan.detail: Change the filter to always report, or always drop. Run the analyzer tests in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests and check that existing MsgPack003/004/005 tests still fail or pass as expected. A surviving mutant would show the filter is untested.

hunches.claim: The three source fixes at the DeclaringSyntaxReferences sites are masked by the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper, and the tests only assert no diagnostics. Reverting any single site fix (restoring [0]) would still crash, but removing the wrapper alone would not be detected as long as the locations are null. More importantly, no test asserts the diagnostic is still reported for in-source types, so the wrapper could drop all diagnostics and tests would still pass.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1444 negate-condition: if (!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || ContainsSyntaxTree) -> if (false); expected to survive because the new tests only assert zero diagnostics, and existing analyzer tests are not in the diff

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation has no positive test: nothing checks that a diagnostic with an in-compilation source location (e.g. MsgPack004 on a same-assembly generic struct) is still reported, nor that a diagnostic with Location.None is still reported. Mutating the guard to always drop would not fail any test in the diff.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1444 remove-guard: report(diagnostic) inside the if -> delete-statement; expected to survive because every new test expects zero diagnostics

hunches.claim: The MemberNeedsKey fix (FirstOrDefault) is exercised only by the UnkeyedMember test, but the test cannot tell whether the crash was avoided by the FirstOrDefault change or by the wrapper. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull site (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) has no test at all: no test has a metadata property with a [Key] whose int and string key are both null.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: replace GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) with item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]... ; expected to survive because no test reaches the both-keys-null branch for a metadata type

hunches.claim: The generated-resolver assertion only checks that the hint name exists. It does not check that the resolver actually registers a formatter for the closed generic struct, and the main verification test skips the generated-sources check (SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck), so the output content is unverified.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator on the usage compilation and inspect the resolver content for the closed generic struct; the current Assert.Contains on hint name would pass with an empty resolver

hunches.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites in `TypeCollector` (reporter's lines 735, 1009 and 1101). The diff guards only two of them, the MsgPack property-key diagnostic at line 985 and MemberNeedsKey at line 1077. No hunk touches the earlier site inside `GetObjectInfo` (around reporter line 735). If that site still indexes `[0]` on head, it can still throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` for metadata symbols. That would leave unmet the criterion that diagnostics needing a source location do not crash for symbols without declaring syntax.

receipt_plan.detail: On head, run `grep -n "DeclaringSyntaxReferences\[0\]" src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs`; any remaining hit inside GetObjectInfo is unguarded. Then run Req2283ReferencedGenericStructTests on head; a failure in either theory row shows the crash path is still live.

hunches.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose source tree is not in the current compilation, and the wrapper is installed for all diagnostics. Diagnostics for metadata members are now silently suppressed rather than prevented. The ledger (L8) says missing diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are not defects, so this is probably fine. The remaining risk is a diagnostic that protects users from an insecure configuration, such as MsgPack007/008 or a custom-formatter misuse, being dropped if its location is in a tree from another compilation. That is unlikely, because such locations come from the compilation's own syntax. No concrete security regression was found.

receipt_plan.detail: Read ReportIfLocatedInCompilation and confirm that diagnostics with Location.None (IsInSource false) still pass through, and that only foreign-tree diagnostics are dropped. No security setting such as MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData or MaximumObjectGraphDepth is touched.

hunches.claim: The new test helper asserts no diagnostics only for the generator run, using LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3 by default for the struct tests. The new docs claim that record structs and generic value types are supported. The record struct test passes the generator test only with Latest. Nothing verifies that the generated resolver content, rather than only its hint name, handles Item<int> correctly. SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck is also set.

receipt_plan.detail: Read RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync: it asserts only that the hint name exists, and SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck skips content verification. Compile the generated output to see whether Item<int> gets a formatter.

hunches.claim: The third crash site mentioned by the reporter (~line 1101, GetParameterListLocation / constructor diagnostics) is not covered by any test, and the diff shows no change there. The tests only cover property members, with no metadata type that has a constructor-related diagnostic path.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs ~line 1101 and the surrounding diagnostic code still index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]; no test hits it

residual_risk: This change touches 4 files (0 generated) in tests, type-collector; the highest routed risk is 7/10. 1 file(s) were routed for deep review, 3 for light review and 0 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 170 passed, 1 failed. 11 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. 3 thing(s) were not checked, including compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes); tests/MessagePack.Tests and other runtime test suites; NativeAOT, Unity and non-net8.0 target frameworks. By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.
